results.question: what are your rally scoring rules
results.answer:
For LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League rally scoring:

- A team can win a point whether serving or receiving, except for the game-winning point.
- If the serving team loses a rally, it is a side out; the receiving team earns a point and takes over serve.
- After a side out, the first server is based on that team’s score: right side serves if the score is even; left side serves if odd.
- Players switch sides only after winning a point on their own serve, and the same player continues serving from the new side.
- Scoring freezes when a team reaches one point below the game-winning score. That team can score the winning point only while serving.
- In win-by-two games, if the score is tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, both teams unfreeze and normal rally scoring resumes until a team again reaches a score where its next point would win by two. The game-winning point must always be scored while serving.

selected.content:
• Service Positioning: After a side out, the first serve is determined by the team's
score: the player on the right (baseline facing the net) serves if the score is even, and
the player on the left serves if the score is odd.

• Switching Sides: Players only switch sides after winning a point on their own serve.
The same player continues serving from the new side.

• Side Outs & Scoring: If the serving team loses a rally, a side out occurs; the
opposing team earns a point and takes over the serve.

• Game Points: A team can win a point regardless of whether they are serving or
receiving except for the winning point (see next item).

• Scoring Freeze and Match Point: To keep the game competitive through the final
point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,
a team’s score shall initially freeze at 24. The scoring freeze applies only to the team
that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using
normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches the applicable freeze point. A team must
be serving to score the game-winning point.

• Win-by-Two (2) Games: When the game is played using a win-by-two (2) format
and the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, neither team can
win by scoring the next point. Therefore, both teams’ scores shall become
unfrozen, and normal Rally Scoring shall resume. Thereafter, a team’s score shall
freeze again whenever it reaches a score at which its next point would win the

game by two (2) points. If the score becomes tied again, both teams shall again
become unfrozen. This freeze-and-unfreeze process shall continue as necessary
until one team wins the game by two (2) points. The game-winning point must
always be scored while serving.

results.question: Is the kitchen the same as the NVZ
results.answer: Yes. In this context, “kitchen” means the non-volley zone (NVZ). The NVZ is the 7-foot by 20-foot area adjacent to each end of the net, and all lines bounding it are part of the zone.

net. The non-volley zone lines run parallel to the net, 7
feet (2.13 m) from the net on each end between the

are part of the zone. The non-volley zone is two-
dimensional and does not extend above the playing

6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

results.question: I am unable to log into my account. How do I reset my password
results.answer:
Click **Forgot Password** on the LMS login screen. Enter the email address associated with your Club Membership; a setup/password reset email will be sent from **no-reply@auth.lwrpickleballclub.com**.

results.question: Can I stand in the kitchen when I am not volleying?
results.answer: Yes. You may stand in the kitchen/non-volley zone when you are not volleying. The restriction is that all volleys must be initiated outside the non-volley zone, and you may contact the non-volley zone at any time except during the act of volleying a ball.

results.question: What kind of games will be played in the Saturday League?
results.answer:
The Saturday League plays men’s doubles, women’s doubles, and mixed doubles games.

- Men’s Round Robin: 3 men’s teams; each player plays 3 games.
- Women’s Round Robin: 3 women’s teams; each player plays 3 games.
- Mixed Round: 6 mixed teams; each player plays 1 mixed game.
- If the match is tied 12-12 after gender and mixed doubles, a Picklebreaker is played using the same mixed teams.

All regular games are to 15 using rally scoring, win by 1. The Picklebreaker, if needed, is one game to 25, win by 2, using rally scoring.

selected.content:
Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four
gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin.
Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams. If the match is tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed
doubles, the Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’
designated order.

6.2.3.1. All Games: Games to 15 using Rally Scoring* (win by 1). 1 point per win. Two
one-minute timeouts per team/game but no timeouts in Picklebreaker. Teams
switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points. Visitors choose serve,
receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.

6.2.3.2. Men's Round Robin: 3 Men’s teams play Round Robin (from low to high,
Teams 1 to 3). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.

6.2.3.3. Women's Round Robin: 3 Women’s teams play Round Robin (from low to
high, Teams 4 to 6). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.

6.2.3.4. Mixed Round: Create 6 Mixed teams (from low to high, Teams 7 to 12). Each
player will play 1 mixed game. 6 points possible.

6.2.3.5. Picklebreaker™ Game (Only played if tie at the end of all previous rounds -
12-12): Features all the mixed teams that played in the Mixed rounds. This will

be one game to 25 win by 2 using Rally Scoring. The winning team collects 3
additional points. (If there isn’t a tie, the leading team collects a 3-point
bonus.) Note: Picklebreaker matches will not be recorded in DUPR and do not
reflect on individual’s W/L record.
Teams are numbered 1–3 for Men’s Doubles, 4–6 for Women’s Doubles, and 7–12 for Mixed
Doubles. These team numbers correspond directly to the Match Score Sheet printed from the system.
We highly recommend assigning higher team numbers to teams with higher combined skill levels and
ratings (for instance, Team 6 should have a higher combined DUPR rating than Team 4 in Women’s or
Team 12 should be a higher team rating than Team 7 in Mixed Doubles).

6.2.4. Scoring: A maximum of 27 total possible match points per date. This includes 24
possible points awarded during standard play, plus a 3-point bonus. If the match
ends in a tie after the mixed doubles division (12-12), a Picklebreaker will be played
to determine the winner of the 3 bonus points. If there is no tie, the leading team
automatically receives the 3-point bonus.

results.question: What is the Saturday match format?
results.answer:
The Saturday DUPR League match format is:

- All games are to 15 using rally scoring, win by 1. Each win is worth 1 point.
- Each team gets two one-minute timeouts per game, but no timeouts in the Picklebreaker.
- Teams switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points.
- Visitors choose serve, receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.
- Men’s round robin: 3 men’s teams, Teams 1–3, each player plays 3 games; 9 points possible.
- Women’s round robin: 3 women’s teams, Teams 4–6, each player plays 3 games; 9 points possible.
- Mixed round: 6 mixed teams, Teams 7–12, each player plays 1 mixed game; 6 points possible.
- The schedule uses two courts for men and two courts for women; after the first four gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin, and Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams.
- If tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed doubles, a Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’ designated order. It is one game to 25, win by 2, using rally scoring, and the winner gets 3 additional points. If there is no tie, the leading team gets a 3-point bonus.
- Picklebreaker matches are not recorded in DUPR and do not count toward an individual’s win/loss record.

6.3.3. Match Format: Teams play Round Robin. 2 out of 3 to 11 (win by 2). Plus, potential
Picklebreaker to 15 (win by 2 using Rally Scoring).
